cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.21)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lodestone - Shared SKSE framework (Phase 16)
# Stage A: validation plugin. Just writes a line to the SKSE log.
# Stage B: per-module infrastructure + Papyrus API (Lodestone.GetVersion).
# Stage C.1 Part 1.5: CastTime module, TRACE ONLY (logs, changes nothing).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the DLL version.
# These numbers feed three consumers:
#   1. The SKSE plugin version boilerplate (generated by add_commonlibsse_plugin)
#   2. The load log line
#   3. Lodestone.GetVersion() / GetVersionString() on the Papyrus side (via Version.h)
# DLL version - INDEPENDENT of the mod version on Nexus.
project(
    Lodestone
    VERSION 1.19.0
    LANGUAGES CXX
)

# CommonLibSSE-NG requires C++23.
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version.h generated from src/Version.h.in (Stage B.1).
# @ONLY: only expands @VAR@, ignores ${VAR} - keeps CMake from touching C++ code.
# Generated file goes to the binary dir (build artifact, not versioned).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
configure_file(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/Version.h.in"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated/Version.h"
    @ONLY
)

# CommonLibSSE-NG comes from the git submodule at extern/commonlibsse-ng
# (alandtse/CommonLibVR, branch ng, pinned to a release tag).
#
# It used to be resolved via find_package against the colorglass vcpkg registry,
# pinned at 3.5.3 - the CharmedBaryon line, abandoned upstream (its successor's
# README declares that vcpkg port unmaintained). The alandtse fork has no vcpkg
# port; the path its README documents is a git submodule plus vcpkg for the
# transitive dependencies (spdlog, directxtk, rapidcsv - see vcpkg.json), which
# is what this does. Consumption pattern follows the pinned tag's own
# test_consumer/CMakeLists.txt.
#
# BUILD_TESTS is the submodule's option (default ON); its tests need catch2 and
# are not ours to run, so force it off before add_subdirectory sees the option.
set(BUILD_TESTS OFF CACHE BOOL "Disable CommonLibSSE-NG tests in consumer" FORCE)
add_subdirectory(extern/commonlibsse-ng EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)

# add_commonlibsse_plugin lives in this file. The submodule's source-build path
# does not include it itself (only its prebuilt path does), so the consumer
# includes it explicitly after add_subdirectory.
include(extern/commonlibsse-ng/cmake/CommonLibSSE.cmake)

# SafetyHook - inline detours for NON-VIRTUAL engine functions.
#
# WHY A SECOND HOOKING MECHANISM EXISTS. CommonLibSSE's Trampoline::write_branch
# does not detour a function body: it assumes the address already holds a 5-byte
# rel32 branch, decodes that displacement, and returns the branch's original
# target. It is a tool for redirecting an existing CALL SITE. Pointed at a
# prologue it returns an address in no loaded module, and the first call through
# it crashes the game - which is exactly what happened here before this was
# understood.
#
# Detouring a function body requires relocating the displaced prologue, which
# requires knowing instruction boundaries and rewriting rip-relative operands.
# That is disassembler work; SafetyHook does it (via Zydis) and additionally
# suspends other threads while patching, which matters in a game with a render
# thread and a script VM running concurrently.
#
# THE RULE, so this does not drift:
#   virtual function      -> vtable swap (REL::Relocation::write_vfunc)
#   non-virtual function  -> SafetyHook inline hook
#   Trampoline::write_branch -> NOT USED. Only valid on a call site, and every
#                               use of it in this project was on a function body.
#
# PINNED BY OVERRIDE in vcpkg.json, not by the baseline: safetyhook is absent
# from the pinned builtin-baseline, and moving that baseline would re-resolve
# every other dependency of a project that builds clean. The override keeps the
# rest of the dependency set frozen - which also means bumping the baseline will
# NOT bump safetyhook. That is deliberate; change it in vcpkg.json explicitly.
find_package(safetyhook CONFIG REQUIRED)

# add_commonlibsse_plugin creates the DLL target, wires up CommonLibSSE linkage,
# and auto-generates the SKSE version boilerplate (SKSEPlugin_Version).
# Output file will be Lodestone.dll.
add_commonlibsse_plugin(
    ${PROJECT_NAME}
    AUTHOR "Awrawra"
    SOURCES
        src/plugin.cpp
        src/Core/Log.cpp
        src/Core/Papyrus.cpp
        src/Core/PluginInfo.cpp
        src/Core/MultiChannel.cpp
        src/Core/ChannelInfo.cpp
        src/Core/CastTime.cpp
        src/Core/BookFramework.cpp
        src/Core/SpellTomes.cpp
        src/Core/MagicScaling.cpp
        src/Core/Detection.cpp
        src/Core/DetectionRead.cpp
        src/Core/Incapacitation.cpp
        src/Core/Serialization.cpp
        src/Core/WebUIBridge.cpp
        src/Core/PrismaUIBackend.cpp
        src/Core/EquipVeto.cpp
)

target_compile_features(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE cxx_std_23)

# /utf-8 - required by the vendored Meridian UI API headers, which carry UTF-8
# bytes (em dashes and a multiplication sign) inside their doc comments. Without
# it MSVC reads the source as the system codepage, and on a non-UTF-8 locale
# those bytes decode to mojibake or raise C4819. Meridian's own author guide
# names this flag as a requirement for consuming its headers.
#
# This does NOT relax the project's own ASCII rule: our sources stay ASCII, and
# check_ascii.py skips extern/ anyway. The flag exists for the third-party bytes
# we are not allowed to edit.
target_compile_options(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE "$<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>:/utf-8>")

target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE safetyhook::safetyhook)

# Where the generated Version.h is found by #include "Version.h", and where the
# two web UI backends' API headers are found.
#
# The two are NOT tracked the same way, and the difference is licensing, not
# preference:
#
#   extern/prismaui-api/     NOT tracked. The Prisma UI License is proprietary
#                            and source-available, and adds restrictions this
#                            GPL-3.0-only repository cannot carry. Copy the
#                            header in by hand before building - the README in
#                            that folder says from where.
#   extern/meridianui-api/   TRACKED. Meridian UI's API headers are plain MIT,
#                            which adds no restriction, so they are vendored
#                            with their LICENSE-MIT alongside.
#
# Neither backend is a dependency: both are detected at runtime and the bridge
# falls through to sentinels when neither is installed.
target_include_directories(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/extern/prismaui-api"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/extern/meridianui-api"
)

# PCH.h is mandatory for CommonLibSSE-NG. Force-included in every file of the
# target, it brings in the CommonLib headers before Relocation.h gets parsed.
# add_commonlibsse_plugin already applies /Zc:preprocessor and other required flags.
target_precompile_headers(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE src/PCH.h)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Copies the DLL to the MO2 deploy mod after each build (Stage B).
#
# The deploy folder is NOT a worktree of anything - it's only a destination for
# the compiled artifact, outside git. Source lives in this repo; the compiled
# binary lives there. Never the other way around.
#
# Enabled in Stage B to remove manual copying: forgetting to copy makes the
# game load the stale DLL, and the resulting bug looks like a code issue.
#
# LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER is overridable: pass -DLODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER=... on
# the CMake command line, or set it in the environment. A contributor's deploy
# path is not ours to hardcode, so the default below is only a fallback used
# when neither is provided. Set it to an empty string to skip deploy entirely.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(NOT DEFINED LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER AND DEFINED ENV{LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER})
    set(LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER "$ENV{LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}")
endif()

if(NOT DEFINED LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER)
    set(LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER "G:/Modlists/Skyrim Dev/mods/Lodestone - DEV/SKSE/Plugins")
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plugin configuration - deployed ONCE, then left alone.
#
# src/Core/EquipVeto.cpp reads Data\SKSE\Plugins\Lodestone.ini for its
# diagnostics. A user edits that file, so copying it on every build would
# throw those edits away, and not copying it at all would mean hand-creating a
# file in the deploy folder - which is where the compiled artifact lives and
# where nothing is authored.
#
# The guard is the whole point: the template lands only if there is nothing
# there yet.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER AND NOT EXISTS "${LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}/Lodestone.ini")
    configure_file(
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/Lodestone.ini"
        "${LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}/Lodestone.ini"
        COPYONLY
    )
    message(STATUS "Config template deployed: ${LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}/Lodestone.ini")
endif()

if(LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER)
    message(STATUS "DLL deploy folder: ${LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}")
    add_custom_command(
        TARGET ${PROJECT_NAME}
        POST_BUILD
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E make_directory "${LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}"
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
            "$<TARGET_FILE:${PROJECT_NAME}>" "${LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}"
        VERBATIM
    )
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compiles and deploys the Papyrus surface (src/Lodestone.psc -> Lodestone.pex,
# plus the .psc source itself) to the same mod folder as the DLL, after each
# build. Consumers never need their own copy of the script - Scripts/ and
# Scripts/Source/ land as siblings of SKSE/, the layout every consumer's
# import path already expects.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. The DLL deploy above already existed; the Papyrus side did
# not, and that gap caused a real bug: a session that only rebuilt the DLL had
# it deployed automatically, while the installed .psc/.pex stayed stale, and a
# consumer's own build gate (reading the installed .psc) failed to find
# natives that were, in fact, already in the DLL. Compiling and copying both
# artifacts from the same POST_BUILD step ties them to one trigger, so a
# fresh DLL next to a stale Papyrus surface cannot happen again.
#
# LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER is overridable the same way LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER
# is above: a contributor's Skyrim install path is not ours to hardcode, so the
# default below is only a fallback. If the compiler is not found at that path,
# this step is skipped with a message instead of failing the native build -
# a missing Papyrus toolchain is an environment gap, not a C++ build error.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(NOT DEFINED LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER AND DEFINED ENV{LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER})
    set(LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER "$ENV{LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER}")
endif()

if(NOT DEFINED LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER)
    set(LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER "G:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Skyrim Special Edition/Papyrus Compiler/PapyrusCompiler.exe")
endif()

if(LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER AND EXISTS "${LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER}")
    # LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER is .../<mod>/SKSE/Plugins - strip two levels to
    # reach the mod's own root, so Scripts/ lands as SKSE/'s sibling.
    get_filename_component(_lodestoneSkseFolder "${LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER}" DIRECTORY)
    get_filename_component(_lodestoneModRoot "${_lodestoneSkseFolder}" DIRECTORY)
    set(LODESTONE_SCRIPTS_FOLDER "${_lodestoneModRoot}/Scripts")

    # Base-game import paths - Lodestone.psc itself imports nothing beyond
    # native Skyrim types, but the compiler still needs these on the search
    # path to resolve Actor, Form, Alias and the rest of the base types.
    set(_lodestoneGameScriptsSource "G:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Skyrim Special Edition/Data/Scripts/Source")
    set(_lodestoneGameSourceScripts "G:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Skyrim Special Edition/Data/Source/Scripts")

    message(STATUS "Papyrus deploy folder: ${LODESTONE_SCRIPTS_FOLDER}")
    add_custom_command(
        TARGET ${PROJECT_NAME}
        POST_BUILD
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E make_directory "${LODESTONE_SCRIPTS_FOLDER}/Source"
        COMMAND "${LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER}"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/Lodestone.psc"
            -f=TESV_Papyrus_Flags.flg
            "-i=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src;${_lodestoneGameScriptsSource};${_lodestoneGameSourceScripts}"
            "-o=${LODESTONE_SCRIPTS_FOLDER}"
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/Lodestone.psc" "${LODESTONE_SCRIPTS_FOLDER}/Source/Lodestone.psc"
        VERBATIM
    )
elseif(LODESTONE_OUTPUT_FOLDER)
    message(STATUS "Papyrus deploy skipped: compiler not found at "
                    "\"${LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER}\" (set LODESTONE_PAPYRUS_COMPILER to override).")
endif()
